steps.title: Key Features
steps.body: A good speech is memorable, persuasive, and connects emotionally with the audience. It uses rhetorical devices to create impact and is designed to be heard, not just read.

steps.title: Key idea 2
steps.body: Introduction (Opening): Hook: Start with a striking statement, question, or anecdote Establish your credibility and purpose Connect with your audience

steps.title: Key idea 3
steps.body: Main Body: Present 3-4 key points Use one paragraph per point Support with evidence and examples Include rhetorical devices throughout Address counter-arguments if needed

steps.title: Key idea 4
steps.body: Conclusion (Ending): Summarise your main message End with a powerful call to action Leave a lasting impression

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What is the purpose of a "hook" in a speech opening? | Name three rhetorical devices commonly used in speeches. | Write an opening paragraph for a speech about the importance of voting.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A hook grabs the audience's attention immediately, making them want to listen. It could be a question, striking statement, or anecdote. | Rhetorical questions, repetition, rule of three, emotive language, direct address, imperatives - any three of these. | Your opening should include: a greeting, a hook (question or statement), direct address, and clear indication of the topic.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Start with a strong hook - grab attention immediately Use direct address throughout: "we", "you", "us" Include a range of rhetorical devices Vary your sentence lengths for rhythm and impact End with a powerful, memorable conclusion Include a clear call to action Read your work aloud to check it sounds like a speech
